name: Live at the Crucible
genre: Live Stadium Rock / 1980s AOR / Progressive Symphonic Space-Rock / Collegiate Marching Band Rock
description: The band's most important live album. Recorded live on Saturday, May 21, 2016 inside The Crucible in Blacksburg, Virginia—Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute's 65,000-seat stadium and the loudest house in all of college football—and released commercially during CPI Homecoming Weekend on October 15, 2016. With no opening act, CPI Alumni (Class of 1989) return home for a seven-act, 34-track career-spanning stadium show marking the final concert of a touring The Stardust Engine before launching their annual Forger Nation Summer Festival residency in Blacksburg in August 2017. Opens with the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers ('Ignition: The Forger's Call', 'CPI Tech Triumph', and 'The Stardust Engine'), includes the ONLY recorded live performance of Cassidy's 13-minute magnum opus 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' anchoring the 10-song Twin Moons cosmic journey (Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock + Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98), an intimate four-song acoustic block pairing Our Own Frequency with a stripped-down piano-and-acoustic-guitar rendition of 'Still Your Safe Person', the live concert debut of 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible', a hometown singalong on 'Neon on the Huckleberry Trail', a false ending on 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street', and the secret 5:26 1980s Stadium Rock (AOR) closing reclamation of 'Electric Color'.
subtitle: 3-Disc Live Box Set • Recorded Live Inside The Crucible (May 21, 2016) • Released Homecoming Weekend at the CPI Campus Bookstore (October 15, 2016)
linerNotes: Thirty years after four CPI undergraduates and their sixteen-year-old younger sister in a Progress Street garage won a 1986 student contest with a raw cassette tape—and sixteen-year-old Holly O'Connell protected it with her famous $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License—The Stardust Engine returned home to Blacksburg on Saturday, May 21, 2016 to take the stage inside The Crucible, the 65,000-seat concrete-and-Ironstone fortress of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) football. There was no opening act—just CPI Alumni (Class of 1989) coming home to play a full seven-act, 34-track career retrospective for their alma mater.

At the heart of the stadium show is the 10-song Twin Moons cosmic centerpiece (Acts III & IV), turning the open-air bowl of The Crucible into the Engine Room Records Planetarium under the Appalachian stars. Act III (Cosmic Tidal Lock — Cassidy's Zero-G Orbit) opens in astrophysical launch order with the 13-minute-3-second Live Album Premiere of Cassidy O'Connell's four-movement magnum opus, 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)'—making Live at the Crucible the ONLY live album where you can experience 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' live—followed by 'Apoapsis', 'Second Apoapsis', 'The Spectrum (True Color)', and 'Moon 1: Tidal Lock'. Act IV (Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98 — Ryan's Heavy-Friction Orbit) answers with a matching 5-song counterbalance ('Moon 2: Roche Limit', 'Impact [Mile Marker 98]', 'Mayday: The Intercept', 'Star City: Orbital Ward', and 'Twin Moons: Touchdown') before Evan and Tyler step offstage for Act V's Our Own Frequency living-room acoustic block, where Ryan and Cassidy introduce 'Brother's Keeper' by announcing the end of global road touring and the launch of the annual Forger Nation Summer Festival residency in Blacksburg in August 2017, and flow from 2008's 'Safe Person' directly into a stripped-down piano-and-acoustic-guitar rendition of 2015's 'Still Your Safe Person'.

Pressed as a flagship 3-Disc Red Book Digital Audio CD Box Set (164:35 base musical runtime across 34 tracks, plus live stage transitions and ovations) and 4K Concert Blu-ray for CPI Homecoming Weekend on October 15, 2016—with pallet stacks debuting at midnight inside the CPI Campus Bookstore and bundled with the bonus 16-track 30th-Anniversary archival companion compilation The Forger's Call (bookended by the 1986 Crucible Stadium Version and 1986 Progress Street 'Demo Take 3' of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call', also available separately)—each disc is engineered around the 74-minute Red Book CD standard so no continuous musical suite is ever interrupted: Disc 1 ('Terrestrial Velocity: The Alma Mater Opening & Reignition', Tracks 1–11, 44:01 base runtime) captures the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers opener and the high-energy Reignition/Vault block up to the stadium floodlight blackout after 'Steel and Synthetics'; Disc 2 ('Ad Astra: The Twin Moons Live Suite', Tracks 1–10, 60:59 base runtime) houses the entire unbroken 10-track progressive space-opera from 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' through 'Twin Moons: Touchdown'; and Disc 3 ('Our Own Frequency & Saturday Night Lights: The Homecoming Finale', Tracks 1–13, 59:35 base runtime) opens in pin-drop silence with the four-song acoustic sanctuary set and Forger Nation Summer Festival announcement before roaring through 'Saturday Night Lights', 'Progress Street', 'Neon on the Huckleberry Trail', 'My Anchor Holds', the 'Last Bus Home' false ending, and the 300-piece Marching Forgers stadium-rock finale of 'Electric Color'.

studioArchives.title: Act I: The 3-Song Alma Mater Opening with the CPI Marching Forgers
studioArchives.content: Before May 21, 2016, the only way to hear 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' was to attend a CPI Home Football Game in person inside The Crucible. For the opening of Live at the Crucible, all 300 members of the CPI Marching Forgers ('The Engine Room' Kevlar snare battery and full brass line) take the field with the band for (1) the first-ever recorded live concert performance of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call', (2) the CPI Fight Song 'CPI Tech Triumph: The Marching Forgers', and (3) a massive brass-and-synth rendition of the band's traditional concert opener, 'The Stardust Engine', before the Marching Forgers exit the tunnel—seemingly for the night.

studioArchives.title: Act III: "Cosmic Tidal Lock" & The 13:03 Live Premiere of "Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"
studioArchives.content: Live at the Crucible is the ONLY live album in The Stardust Engine's catalog to feature Cassidy O'Connell's four-movement progressive symphonic rock suite, 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' (13:03). Sequenced in Astrophysical Launch Order to open Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock, all four stadium floodlight towers cut to black as Cassidy leads 65,000 fans from the trauma of the 1992 Friction trial ('Part I: The Cage') through the roaring rocket liftoff of 'Part II: Ignition (Ad Astra)', across the mid-track Main Engine Cutoff ovation at 06:30 into the weightless nebula of 'Part III: The Cosmos', and finally into the splashdown of 'Part IV: Re-entry (The New World)'—where 65,000 Forgers roar 'HELD BY THE SUN!' in unison before Cassidy whispers a breathless 'Thank you so much...' (bringing her 1990 'If You Walked Away' journey full circle). From there, the vessel coasts upward through 'Apoapsis', 'Second Apoapsis', and 'The Spectrum (True Color)' before locking into 'Moon 1: Tidal Lock'.

studioArchives.title: Act IV: "Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98" — Ryan's 5-Song Heavy-Friction Counterbalance
studioArchives.content: Directly answering Cassidy's five-song Zero-G orbit in Act III, Ryan O'Connell takes the helm for a matching five-song hard-rock block drawn from Disc 2 of 1997's Hard Reset and his 2003 solo-led concept album Mile Marker 98 ('Moon 2: Roche Limit', 'Impact [Mile Marker 98]', 'Mayday: The Intercept', 'Star City: Orbital Ward', and 'Twin Moons: Touchdown'). Translating the December 10, 1990 Interstate 81 Mile Marker 98 crash, his complete T10 spinal cord injury, and the strict 4-hour survival clock of 'Protocol T-10' into a high-friction cosmic collision and family rescue mission, Act IV brings both Twin Moons safely down on solid ground in Blacksburg right before the acoustic living-room block.

studioArchives.title: Act V: The "Our Own Frequency" Acoustic Block, "Brother's Keeper", "Still Your Safe Person" & The Forger Nation Summer Festival Residency
studioArchives.content: In 2008, during the middle of their Burnout Hiatus, Ryan and Cassidy recorded Our Own Frequency in complete secrecy in the living room of the Blacksburg house with just an acoustic guitar, a piano, and two microphones—never touring it, simply uploading it on a Tuesday morning with the one-sentence note: 'We're still here, and we're okay.' In Act V, Evan and Tyler leave the stage so brother and sister can share those deeply private songs live for the very first time ('Our Own Frequency', 'Brother's Keeper', and 'Safe Person'), followed immediately by a stripped-down acoustic grand piano and fingerpicked guitar rendition of 2015's 'Still Your Safe Person' as the seven-year living-room sequel to 'Safe Person'. Introducing the centerpiece 'Brother's Keeper'—an unflinchingly intimate look at how Cassidy and the family perform Ryan's daily ADLs (toileting, morning anti-atrophy leg stretches, and Cassidy sleeping on the outside edge of the bed pushed against the wall as a human bed-rail so Ryan doesn't roll off) while Ryan acts as her emotional anchor—Ryan explains why twenty-six years after the 1990 crash, the physical toll of those daily routines on the road makes tonight the last concert of a touring The Stardust Engine, and Cassidy unveils the annual Forger Nation Summer Festival launching in August 2017.

studioArchives.title: The Sacred Rule of "Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible" & How Forger Nation Claimed "Neon on the Huckleberry Trail"
studioArchives.content: Although the studio master of 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible' premiered over the stadium PA between the 3rd and 4th quarters on October 8, 2004, The Stardust Engine never performed the song on a concert stage until this May 21, 2016 homecoming—honoring their permanent vow that 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible' will ONLY ever be played live when performing inside The Crucible. That fourth-quarter sprint flows straight into 'Progress Street: Where the Fire Began' and 'Neon on the Huckleberry Trail'—a deep album cut from 2015's Reignition that cuts so close to home that the Crucible audience spontaneously hijacks it and makes it their own. While out-of-towners in the stands don't know the local geography, every Forger knows the six-mile paved path from the Pendleton Library lawn to Christiansburg, and older alumni who fondly remember the historic Huckleberry Train (which ran until 1958) join 20-year-old undergrads in a 65,000-voice takeover as Cassidy and Ryan step back from their microphones in awe.

studioArchives.title: Operation Anvil: The "Last Bus Home" False Ending & The 1:40 Reveal of "Electric Color"
studioArchives.content: At the close of Act VI, the band staged 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street' as a convincing false ending—turning the stage switches off and plunging the stadium into darkness so the audience believed the stadium show was over. Then, in the pitch dark, all 300 members of the CPI Marching Forgers marched back onto the stage to join the band for Act VII: a secret 5-minute-26-second 1980s AOR Stadium Rock reclamation of 'Electric Color' (protected all semester by Holly's $300,000 student escrow and Cassidy's 'Exercise 87-B' decoy charts). Because the 77-second AOR guitar and 300-horn brass overture sounds nothing like the 1987 Dance Synth-Pop single, not even fans in Section 104, Row A recognized the song until 1:40 on the dot, when Cassidy belted: 'Woke up this morning, the world was gray...'

studioArchives.title: For Forgers, By Forgers: The $15M Scalper Lockout & Zero Backing Tracks
studioArchives.content: Under Addendum No. 3 to her 1986 Cross-License, Holly O'Connell walked away from an estimated $12M–$15M+ in dynamic-pricing stadium gross by buying out all ~35,000 Field Level and Lower Bowl seats upfront and selling them AT COST through CPI's Zero-Knowledge SAML 2.0 Poly Pass portal. On stage, because the band strictly refuses to use pre-recorded backing tracks, the core four-piece family is backed on the stage-left riser by their 5-piece 'Orbital Crew' stadium touring section: Marcus Vance (rhythm guitar/12-string/pedal steel), Darius 'Doc' Holloway (second drum kit/percussion), Claire Lindqvist (auxiliary analog polyphonic synthesizers and tonewheel organ), and CPI Jazz soloists Prof. Julian Vance (trumpet/flugelhorn) and Elena Rostova (tenor/baritone sax).
